checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Three prominent horns: two long brow horns projecting forward and upward above the eyes, and a shorter nasal horn on the snout.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The skeleton clearly displays the characteristic three-horn arrangement: two large supraorbital horns and one smaller nasal horn. The morphology matches the taxonomic description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Beak is parrot-like with a sharp, keratinous cutting edge.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image shows a fossilized skeleton. The 'keratinous cutting edge' refers to soft tissue (beak sheath) which does not preserve in fossils. Only the bony rostral bone is visible, so the checkpoint as described (keratinous edge) is not testable/present.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is quadrupedal with columnar, elephant-like limbs.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The skeletal mount shows four sturdy, columnar limbs supporting the body mass, consistent with quadrupedal ceratopsian anatomy.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Enormous bony frill (neck shield) extending posteriorly from the skull, with width dramatically exceeding the skull itself.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The large parietal-squamosal frill is clearly visible and dominates the posterior aspect of the skull, matching the description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Frill is solid bone with a smooth outer surface and possible epoccipital (marginal) bumps.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The frill appears solid (non-fenestrated) and exhibits the rough texture and marginal ossifications (epoccipitals) typical of Triceratops fossils.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is inferred to have been covered in large, hexagonal scales with possible quill-like structures along the back and tail.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: This is a skeleton; skin and scales are not preserved or present in the image.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Forelimbs are shorter than hindlimbs creating a sloping backline.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The skeletal mount demonstrates the anatomical reality that the forelimbs are shorter than the hindlimbs, resulting in the characteristic downward slope of the dorsal profile towards the head.
The caudal vertebrae visible in the mount are robust and relatively short compared to the body length, consistent with ceratopsian anatomy.
